result.summary: Pausanias describes Theban sacrificial custom and the legend of Cadmus following a cow to found Thebes. He then lists sights in the citadel: the altar of Athene Onga, the ruined chambers of Harmonia and Semele, a statue of Dionysus, and statues of the flute-player Pronomus and Epaminondas.

scenes.title: Sacrifice of oxen to Apollo
scenes.summary: The Thebans explain why they sacrifice working oxen to Apollo Spodius instead of bulls.

scenes.title: Cadmus and the cow
scenes.summary: Cadmus is guided by a marked cow and settles where it lies down; the altar of Athene Onga stands there and is used to argue Cadmus came from Phoenicia.
scenes.stakes: Cadmus and his army need a place to settle, as the oracle commanded.

scenes.title: House of Cadmus and Dionysus
scenes.summary: Pausanias describes the ruined bridal chambers, the sacred wood of Dionysus Cadmus, and the bronze statue of Dionysus.

scenes.title: Pronomus and Epaminondas
scenes.summary: Pronomus's innovations in flute-playing are described, and statues of him and Epaminondas are noted.

alias_notes.explanation: Phoenician name of Athene at Thebes, versus Egyptian Sais.
Name given to the sacred wood adorned by Polydorus.

notable_quotes.reason: Credits Pronomus with a major innovation in flute-playing.

analysis.text: Sacred places in Thebes are tied to founding legends, linking cult practice to Cadmus and his family.
Pausanias uses religious names and etymology to argue over Cadmus's origin, reflecting ancient debates on Greek ties with Phoenicia and Egypt.

legacy.text: The tale of Cadmus following a cow to found Thebes is a classic foundation myth, retold by Ovid and many later writers.

fun_facts.text: Pronomus of Thebes was a real aulos player of the 5th century BC, and the Pronomos Vase is named after him.

language_notes.text: Spodius means "of the ashes"; it is a Theban cult title of Apollo, linked to ash-altars.
Greeks debated whether Cadmus was Egyptian or Phoenician. Sais was the Egyptian city of Neith, whom Greeks identified with Athene; Pausanias argues from the goddess's name.
The Muses' song at the wedding of Harmonia and Cadmus was a famous Theban legend.
Semele, mother of Dionysus, was destroyed by Zeus's lightning when she asked to see him in his glory.
"Measure" means a musical mode or scale; Dorian, Phrygian and Lydian were the main Greek modes.
"Is extant for" means the song survives as one composed for the Chalcidians who went to Delos, presumably for a sacred embassy.

context_notes.text: Cadmus, founder of Thebes, consulted the Delphic oracle, which told him to follow a cow and found a city where it lay down.
Praxiteles was the famous Athenian sculptor; his sons continued his workshop.
Epaminondas was the Theban general who defeated Sparta at Leuctra in 371 BC and made Thebes briefly dominant in Greece.

literary_notes.text: The cow's white flank marks are compared to the full moon, giving the guiding animal a quasi-divine look.
The ruined bridal chambers and the forbidden room of Semele evoke a sense of sacred, lingering myth in the present landscape.
Pronomus is presented as an innovator, defined by being twice "the first" in his art.
